set.body:
Redesign frame, grid, and registry identity without hidden random persistent ids.

Design requirements
- Provide explicit ephemeral, createPersistent(id,...), and restore(record, registry) construction.
- Pure constructors do not generate persistent-looking ids internally.
- FrameKey contains only persistent structural identity: id, spatial rank, length unit, and coordinate convention.
- Frame display metadata is separate and may be renamed without restoration conflict.
- GridKey contains id, frame key/id, shape, and canonical affine data; affine validation tolerance and diagnostics are excluded.
- Registries are immutable values returning an updated registry/resolution, or are explicitly thread-safe with documented mutation.
- Live owner identity, persistent-key identity, exact geometric congruence, and approximate congruence remain separate relations.

Acceptance criteria
- Equivalent derived operations are reproducible under an explicit project identity policy.
- Renaming a frame cannot invalidate structural restoration.
- Constructing the same affine under different validation tolerances cannot create a key conflict.
- Duplicate ids with conflicting structure fail closed.
- Restoring the same key returns checked evidence without conflating distinct live owners.
- No use of scala.util.Random remains in geometry identity creation.

Tests
- Property round trips for FrameKey, GridKey, records, and restore.
- Regression tests for label-only changes and tolerance-only changes.
- Conflict matrix: same id/different rank, unit, convention, frame, shape, or affine.
- Concurrent restore/register stress test with at least 1,000 operations and deterministic outcomes.
- Separate tests for same live owner, same persistent key/different live owner, exact congruence/different key, and approximate congruence.
- JVM/Scala.js parity for keys and canonical record encoding.
- Static tests proving FrameId and GridId remain non-interchangeable.
set.title: Separate ephemeral, persistent, and congruent geometry identity
